title: 26.RTI.OP.102 - Service Framework Contract for the provision of “Nuclear Technologies for EU Defence Energy Systems (NUCLEUS) Study”
description: The present call for tenders aims to award a Framework Contract for the provision of research and consulting services in the form of study in the field of Nuclear Technologies for EU Defence Energy Systems. The general objective of this procurement is to ensure contractual support aimed at addressing emerging questions related to advanced nuclear technologies, defence energy resilience, energy security and the protection of critical energy infrastructure. In order to achieve the objectives of this procurement, EDA intends to award a Framework Contract comprising the following tasks/activities: studies, assessments, expert consultations, workshops and analytical activities related to advanced nuclear technologies, defence energy resilience, energy security, the protection of critical energy infrastructure, regulatory and licensing frameworks, fuel supply considerations, implementation pathways, cyber, hybrid and physical security aspects, and capability development activities.

title: Support to Defence Innovation and Operational Experimentation Activities, including BraveTech EU Testing and Evaluation Campaigns (Phase 2) - Request for information (RFI)/market survey - Information Session: 3 September 2026
description: EDA intends to launch a procurement procedure for a framework service contract covering operational planning, management and execution; technical evaluation support; prize-contest administration; and communication and event services, in support of EDA's defence innovation and operational experimentation activities under the Hub for European Defence Innovation (HEDI). The procurement forms part of the EUDIS BraveTech EU initiative, funded by the EU under the European Defence Fund (EDF) and implemented by EDA under indirect management. Its primary object is the BraveTech EU Testing and Evaluation Campaigns (TECS) (Phase 2), announced on 11 July 2025. Building on the Phase 1 DefTech Forges (European Commission call for tenders EC-DEFIS/2025/OP/0040), Phase 2 comprises 16 Operational Experimentation (OPEX) campaigns in which Phase 1 pre-selected companies test and refine their solutions under operational conditions. Campaigns are governed by a prize-contest mechanism under FR (EU, Euratom) 2024/2509, under which EDA's authorising officer awards prizes of up to EUR 1 000 000 per entity to the best-performing solutions. The contractor(s) shall plan, manage and execute the campaigns on EDA's behalf - including calls for host locations, coordination with host-nation authorities and site operators, logistics, spectrum and safety management, evaluation support, reporting, communication and events, and prize-contest administration - across EU Member States and EDF-associated countries over 2026–2028. The framework contract(s) may also be used to order similar services within the scope and maximum value set out in the procurement documents. The contract is not divided into lots. This notice announces EDA's intention to publish a future call for tenders, an information session for economic operators on 3 September 2026, 10:00–12:00 (CET), and the launch of a market survey (RFI). ++++++++ A. Information Session ( https://forms.office.com/Pages/ResponsePage.aspx?id=X2-UUFRBmkuNd2juNtVUZwsZ5vnJdEJAqruSaWPkOpdUN1VZRTQ2VjZPT1pZQ05QMVRUSkg5MVI4RC4u ) On 3 September 2026, 10:00–12:00 (CET), the European Defence Agency (EDA), through its Hub for European Defence Innovation (HEDI), will hold an Information Session for industry to present the BraveTech EU programme and the Phase 2 procurement approach. The session will cover the procurement strategy and the scope of the forthcoming tender — implementation plan, deliverables, contractual procedures and indicative timeline. The services to be procured cover the operational management of the Operational Experimentation (OPEX) campaigns, including calls for host locations; coordination with host-nation authorities (military or civil) and site operators; logistics and site preparation; spectrum and safety management; technical and operational evaluation support; documentation and reporting; prize-contest administration; and programme communication. The procurement seeks experienced partners to support a large-scale defence technology experimentation programme accelerating the testing, evaluation and operational transition of innovative solutions from European SMEs and start-ups, in response to capability needs identified by EU Member States and Ukraine. More information is provided in Section 2.1.4 "Additional Information" +++++++++++ B. Request for information ( https://ec.europa.eu/eusurvey/runner/Draft_EDA_Survey_on_National_Defence_Testing_Facilities ) In parallel with the Prior Information Notice, EDA is launching a Request for Information (RFI) / Market Survey directed at testing and experimentation centres, ranges, and related facilities established in EU Member States or EDF-associated countries, that may be considered as potential host locations for BraveTech EU OPEX Campaigns under Phase 2. More information is provided in Section 2.1.4 "Additional Information".

The procurement forms part of the EUDIS BraveTech EU initiative, funded by the EU under the European Defence Fund (EDF) and implemented by EDA under indirect management. Building on the Phase 1 DefTech Forges (European Commission call for tenders EC-DEFIS/2025/OP/0040), Phase 2 comprises 16 Operational Experimentation (OPEX) campaigns in which Phase 1 pre-selected companies test and refine their solutions under operational conditions. Campaigns are governed by a prize-contest mechanism under FR (EU, Euratom) 2024/2509, under which EDA's authorising officer awards prizes of up to EUR 1 000 000 per entity to the best-performing solutions. The contractor(s) shall plan, manage and execute the campaigns on EDA's behalf - including calls for host locations, coordination with host-nation authorities and site operators, logistics, spectrum and safety management, evaluation support, reporting, communication and events, and prize-contest administration - across EU Member States and EDF-associated countries over 2026–2028. The framework contract(s) may also be used to order similar services within the scope and maximum value set out in the procurement documents. The contract is not divided into lots. This notice announces EDA's intention to publish a future call for tenders, an information session for economic operators on 3 September 2026, 10:00–12:00 (CET), and the launch of a market survey (RFI). ++++++++ A. description: Categories Prizes Opening date05 May 2026 Closing date04 June 2026 .procurement_downloads { display: none; } PURPOSE OF THE PRIZE CONTESTEDA, through its Hub for European Defence Innovation (HEDI), has launched the Loitering Munitions “Sentinel Strike Challenge”, a Prize Contest designed to support the operational experimentation of emerging loitering munition capabilities in Europe.This initiative aims to:Generate operational evidence: Produce objective and comparable evidence on the performance, resilience, reliability, safety and operational suitability of complete loitering munition systems.Support Member States: Provide trusted evidence to support capability planning, requirement refinement and potential future cooperative activities.Test in realistic conditions: Assess systems in realistic, degraded and contested operational environments.Demonstrate complete systems: Enable selected industry participants to demonstrate full loitering munition systems under controlled military experimentation conditions.Strengthen defence innovation: Bring together operational users, technical experts, industry and national authorities to support Europe’s defence innovation ecosystem. SCOPE OF THE PRIZE CONTESTThe EDA invites applications for the operational experimentation of Class I Aerial Loitering Munitions, with:Maximum take-off mass: up to 25 kgOperational range: up to 40 kmParticipating systems will be assessed across the full precision strike mission cycle, including:Mission planningDeploymentLaunchTarget detection and identificationTarget trackingEngagementPost-strike assessmentThe Challenge will focus on complete loitering munition systems that combine intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance, navigation and precision strike functions within a single capability.PARTICIPATION PROCESSThe Prize Contest is structured in two stages.Stage 1 – Technical Proposal AssessmentEligible applicants will submit technical proposals for evaluation.Up to ten Stage 1 prizes may be awarded.The five highest-ranked Stage 1 winners will be invited to proceed to Stage 2.Stage 2 – Operational Experimentation CampaignSelected participants will deploy and demonstrate their systems during the operational experimentation campaign.Systems will be assessed during field experimentation and through final reports and experimentation results. The campaign is expected to take place in September - October 2026 in Portugal, within the framework of the HEDI Operational Experimentation Campaign 2026, in conjunction with the Portuguese Army’s ARTEX26 technological experimentation exercise. Trials are expected to be conducted at the Santa Margarida Military Training Area, including live-fire demonstrations. TARGET AUDIENCEThe Prize Contest is aimed at eligible industry participants capable of providing and demonstrating complete Class I Aerial Loitering Munition systems.The initiative is particularly relevant for companies developing loitering munition capabilities suitable for operational experimentation in realistic military environments and for observation by European defence stakeholders. IMPORTANT INFORMATIONThis is a Prize Contest, not a standard procurement procedure.The Challenge is intended to provide Member States with reliable, comparable operational evidence on loitering munition capabilities.The maximum total prize budget is EUR 2,000,000, divided as follows:Stage 1 prizes: up to EUR 200,000Stage 2 prizes: up to EUR 1,800,000Applications submitted after the deadline or sent to a different email address will be considered non-admissible.The Rules of Contest with full details, including eligibility requirements, technical admission criteria, award criteria and submission procedures, are available after registration. SUBMISSION DETAILS AND CONTACT POINTApplications must be submitted by email to:Prize.Contest@eda.europa.euThe deadline for receipt of applications is:Thursday, 04 June 2026 at 12:00 Brussels timeThe Prize Contest documentation is available for download through the EDA pre-registration link:Pre-registration for the Sentinel Strike Challenge Prize Contest INDICATIVE TIMETABLEJune 2026: Evaluation of Stage 1 applicationsJuly 2026: Notification of Stage 1 prize winners and invitations to Stage 2September-October 2026: Operational experimentation campaign in PortugalJanuary/February 2027: Award ceremony PROTECTION OF PERSONAL DATAProcessing of personal data for submission purposes is expected to comply with relevant EDA data protection regulations and policies, as further detailed in the Rules of Contest and related procurement documentation. description: The European Defence Agency (EDA), through its Hub for European Defence Innovation (HEDI), is launching a ‘Prize Contest’* as part of the Operational Experimentation Campaign 2026 (OPEX261 PT) in Portugal. The initiative aims to accelerate the development, testing, and operational validation of advanced loitering munition and precision strike systems. Hosted by the Portuguese Army and integrated with the ARTEX26 exercise, the campaign will allow selected participants to demonstrate their technologies in realistic, controlled military environments alongside other emerging systems such as unmanned aerial and ground platforms. The Prize Contest seeks to produce objective performance data aligned with EU Member States’ operational needs, helping identify and mature promising defence technologies for rapid operational adoption. By enabling realistic experimentation, collaboration between industry and military stakeholders and structured technical assessments, the initiative supports informed capability development and future procurement decisions. Ultimately, it aims to strengthen Europe’s defence innovation ecosystem, improve interoperability and enhance the technological readiness and operational effectiveness of European armed forces. The present call for tenders aims to ensure contractual support for the implementation of the above mentioned priorities over a period of four (4) years. The capability development areas to be covered are: - Lot I: GCC - Lot II: FSS - Lot III: LBPE - Lot IV: SAL - Lot V: AM-enabled Military Capabilities - Lot VI: CBRN Defence For each individual LOT I – VI and their respective capability development areas abovementioned, the specific objectives are twofold: - Provision of studies and support for concept development - Provision of event management services

Authority: European Defence Agency
Source: EU Funding & Tenders Portal
Reference: EDA/2026/OP/0001
Title: Framework Service Contracts for the provision of “Support to the implementation of the EU Capability Development Priorities in the Land Domain and for Strategic Enablers” (26.CAP.OP.025)
Publication date: 2026-02-17T00:00:00.000Z
Deadline: 2026-04-10T17:00:59.000Z
Status: CLOSED
Procedure stage: Historical / Closed
Description: The EU Capability Development Priorities endorsed by the EU Ministers of Defence in November 2023 contain three (3) priorities related to the land domain, one (1) priority related to logistics, including AM, and one (1) priority related to CBRN defence: - Ground Combat Capabilities (GCC); - Future Soldier Systems (FSS); - Land Based Precision Engagement (LBPE); - Sustainable and Agile Logistics (SAL); - CBRN Defence. The present call for tenders aims to ensure contractual support for the implementation of the above mentioned priorities over a period of four (4) years. The capability development areas to be covered are: - Lot I: GCC - Lot II: FSS - Lot III: LBPE - Lot IV: SAL - Lot V: AM-enabled Military Capabilities - Lot VI: CBRN Defence For each individual LOT I – VI and their respective capability development areas abovementioned, the specific objectives are twofold: - Provision of studies and support for concept development - Provision of event management services

title: Service Framework Contract for the provision of “Studies on EU Chemicals Legislation and Defence aspects”
description: This contract aims to improve the effectiveness of EDA's coordinating role on chemicals and waste regulation to make a more proactive and comprehensive assessment of the evolving European regulatory framework, to better evaluate the actual impact of new restrictions on chemicals (including indirect ones affecting dual supply chains) on the defence sector, to anticipate necessary mitigating actions, and to develop best apply implementation measures. This contract aims to enhance ongoing monitoring and awareness of broader EU policies that may impact defence capabilities, with a particular focus on chemicals and waste regulations: - Its primary objective is to establish a continuous regulatory monitoring and to assess the implications of evolving legislation on defence and dual-use applications; The second key objective is to provide in-depth analyses of specific chemical-related challenges impacting the defence sector, along with an assessment of potential mitigation measures to avoid compromising defence readiness.

title: MULTI MISSION UNMANNED AIRCRAFT SYSTEM (25.CAP.OP.033)
description: The key objective of the project is to support the development of a fixed-wing Multi Mission Unmanned Aircraft System (M2UAS), capable of performing different types of mission depending on its configuration and/or payloads. This M2UAS concept shall include the feasibility of the different operational capabilities envisaged for the UAS platform (C4ISTAR, ALE , EW, AAR) with a phased approach. The project shall be conceived under a Concept Development and Experimentation (CD&E) approach to prove the concept with different scenarios, and may include system and sub-systems demonstrators. The General Objective is further detailed with the following specific objectives (SO): SO1. Describing the possible conceptual approach and minimum mission requirements for the development of M2UAS, with an initial focus on persistent category (long-endurance missions, platforms, systems and weapons), including fully autonomous systems. SO2. Identifying and analysing technology challenges related to the development of a M2UAS for military purposes, deriving from existing and envisaged platforms and related capabilities. SO3. Detecting the limiting factors for a common UAS platform with different payloads and the levels of effectiveness on different types of missions, focussing on C4ISTAR tasks at operational level. SO4. Recommending principles of systems engineering/design with a focus on assuring the cost effectiveness of the M2UAS with the envisaged capabilities, including the “family concept” of M2UAS depending on the categories (tactical – persistent – penetrating). SO5. Describing the current capability landscape. SO6. Identifying potential collaborative opportunities at EU level, in order to develop M2UAS (e.g. collecting the body of work and needs of MS through workshops). SO7. Involving the Military UAS Operational end-users in the development of M2UAS, from the requirements to the operational experimentation. SO8. Supporting the development of European UAS technology, from the system to the subsystem levels, contributing to European technological superiority in the UAS domain. Presently, it is foreseen to have four specific contracts related to four steps. SC2, SC3 and SC4 themes are merely indicative and might be changed: - SC2 – Building on the results of EDA project FS2CATI-1, this will aim at supporting the development of a concept of operation and operational requirements for a medium size Cargo Drone capability, based on VTOL technologies. - SC3 - Based on the M2UAS concept, this will aim at enabling the capability to deliver Air launched weapons as well as developing EW capability on the same platform. - SC4 - This will concentrate on capability development in the field of automated AAR, based on the M2UAS concept.

title: Service Framework Contract for the provision of “Strategic Analysis of the European Defence Technology Industrial Base (EDTIB) ”
description: The objective of this framework contract is to assist EDA in implementing its Core Task 5, as defined in the EDA’s Long term review 2024. The EDA’s Core Task 5 consists in consolidating and promoting EU Member States’ Ministries of Defence (MoD) common interest towards EU wider policies, both civilian and defence related. EDA contributes to promoting a shared understanding of the legal, technological, and defence challenges to benefit all Member States, industry and EU bodies and agencies. EDA thus contributes to implement current and future strategies and policies, striving to reflect appropriately MoD’s views. This contract aims to support a continuous monitoring and awareness of wider policies affecting the EDTIB, in a fast pace evolving security, policy and economic environment. The overarching goal of this framework contract is to help EDA develop and refine tools and instruments that will support the development of the EDTIB. These are multifaceted and can address all policies that touch upon the activities of the defence industry at the national, intergovernmental and supranational levels.

Status: CLOSED

Description: The objective of this framework contract is to assist EDA in implementing its Core Task 5, as defined in the EDA’s Long term review 2024. The EDA’s Core Task 5 consists in consolidating and promoting EU Member States’ Ministries of Defence (MoD) common interest towards EU wider policies, both civilian and defence related. EDA contributes to promoting a shared understanding of the legal, technological, and defence challenges to benefit all Member States, industry and EU bodies and agencies. EDA thus contributes to implement current and future strategies and policies, striving to reflect appropriately MoD’s views. This contract aims to support a continuous monitoring and awareness of wider policies affecting the EDTIB, in a fast pace evolving security, policy and economic environment. The overarching goal of this framework contract is to help EDA develop and refine tools and instruments that will support the development of the EDTIB. These are multifaceted and can address all policies that touch upon the activities of the defence industry at the national, intergovernmental and supranational levels.

title: Service Framework Contract for the provision of “Support to European Military Airworthiness Requirements (EMAR) Development, Implementation and Training”
description: The overall objective of this call for tenders is the provision of subject matter expertise to support EDA in managing the activities of the MAWA Forum. More specifically, the expertise shall include: a) an in-depth knowledge of the development and content of the EASA regulations (plus their associated supporting documentation); b) adequate knowledge of military aviation environment, including initial certification and continuing airworthiness procedures to be able to provide the MAWA Forum with the specialist advice and guidance needed; c) an understanding of the implications of any military-specific proposals considered during the development of the necessary documents and/or their updates; d) adequate knowledge of the EMAR system applicable to military aviation as well as its specificities compared to the EASA PARTs environment, applicable to civil aviation; e) adequate knowledge in defining military airworthiness certification criteria and airworthiness codes to propose changes and amendments to the EMACC; f) adequate knowledge of civil and military certification procedures, especially in the definition of Type Certification Basis (TCB) to improve the usability of the EMACC Handbook and Guidebook. g) in-depth knowledge of the typical organisation, responsibilities, tasks, staff competence, processes & procedures of an Airworthiness Authority competent in Initial/Continued/Continuing Airworthiness domains.

title: Four Service Contracts (Lots, I, II III & IV) for the provision of “Strategic Research and Innovation Agendas (SRIAs) Updates”
description: The general objective of the present four (4) Direct Contracts is the provision of support to the continued and ongoing development and update of the SRIAs and the TBBs, following the tools and processes developed either for OSRA or for the OSRA toolchain (cf. section 1.4 below). OSRA, which has been in development since January 2016 and is currently developing version 3, establishes a standardized work structure across all CapTechs, integrating a unified vision. Within OSRA v3, a harmonized template guides the development of all SRIAs and the definition of their associated TBBs. The latest version of OSRA also emphasizes the inclusion of an innovation section in the SRIAs. This aims to align the SRIAs with the activities of the recently established Hub for European Defence Innovation (HEDI), ensuring coherence and a more integrated approach. However, OSRA is a living framework. While the methodology applied by the CapTechs to update their SRIAs is fixed, the TBBs will always be subject to evaluation and updates, especially regarding their roadmaps.

Description: The general objective of the present four (4) Direct Contracts is the provision of support to the continued and ongoing development and update of the SRIAs and the TBBs, following the tools and processes developed either for OSRA or for the OSRA toolchain (cf. section 1.4 below). OSRA, which has been in development since January 2016 and is currently developing version 3, establishes a standardized work structure across all CapTechs, integrating a unified vision. Within OSRA v3, a harmonized template guides the development of all SRIAs and the definition of their associated TBBs. The latest version of OSRA also emphasizes the inclusion of an innovation section in the SRIAs. This aims to align the SRIAs with the activities of the recently established Hub for European Defence Innovation (HEDI), ensuring coherence and a more integrated approach. However, OSRA is a living framework. While the methodology applied by the CapTechs to update their SRIAs is fixed, the TBBs will always be subject to evaluation and updates, especially regarding their roadmaps.

title: HUB for EU DEFENCE INNOVATION (HEDI): Technology watch, landscaping - Military Utility Assessment - Market consultation - Defence Innovation Training Courses
description: HEDI’s Defence Future Insights (DFI) provides strategic intelligence on emerging defence technologies by monitoring global R&T trends, weak signals, patent activity, and dual-use innovations. It supports capability-driven prioritisation and long-term defence planning by translating technological insights into defence applications. DFI also assesses innovation ecosystems, identifying key players, readiness levels, and adoption barriers, thus guiding targeted support and informed decision-making for EU defence stakeholders. In parallel, HEDI’s Defence Innovation Course aims to build a shared understanding of defence innovation across EU Ministries of Defence. It delivers practical training for mid-level officers and innovation managers to initiate and manage innovation effectively, addressing capability gaps identified through European Defence Innovation Network (EDIN) and stakeholder consultations. This cluster initiative encompasses four distinct projects, each tackling specific aspects of innovation management: LOT 1: Technology Watch and Landscaping: Provision of a regular and structured AI supported assessment of worldwide technological developments across both defence and non-defence sectors, identifying emerging trends, weak signals, and dual-use innovations that could impact EU security and defence; LOT 2: Military Utility Assessment: Focuses on evaluating the potential military applications of emerging technologies, assessing their operational utility, and identifying pathways for adoption into defence capability development; LOT 3: Consultancy services for needs assessment, market research, and market consultations: Provision of expert consultancy support for conducting market research and facilitating structured market consultations to bridge gaps between innovation suppliers and defence users; LOT 4: Defence Innovation Training Courses: Development and delivery of a structured, high-quality Defence Innovation Course. The first specific contract will focus on an Intermediate Level while potential follow-up contracts will address Basic and Advanced levels. The course is aimed at fostering a harmonized understanding of defence innovation across EU Member States while equipping participants with practical skills for managing and implementing innovation projects within innovation ecosystems. .

title: Service Framework Contract for the provision of “DEFENCE ENERGY MANAGERS’ COURSE II (DEMC II)”
description: The objective of this framework contract is to provide the Member States contributing to the DEMC II Project Arrangement with a developmental educational service specific to the Defence sector and with hands-on application/implementation to specific military sites. The Defence Energy Managers’ Course will increase knowledge and improve energy management in defence, resulting in benefits in terms of energy consumption, cost, and CO2 emission reductions. It should also contribute to reducing exposure to volatile energy prices, improving security of supply, increase operational capabilities, and reduce risk associated with energy supply in the armed forces. Within the Course, an average of two Trainings per year for a period of four years will be delivered. Each of the training editions is, for the purpose of the contract, called a “Training”. For the purpose of these tender specifications, the Defence Sector relates to both Ministries of Defence and Armed Forces and applies to fixed infrastructure, operational environments and military platforms and systems. The aim of the DEMC II Trainings is to enhance participant’s understanding of the complexities of managing energy within an organisation or sub-organisation and illustrate how to structure an effective energy management system and programme. Participants will learn how to systematically, incrementally and continuously improve their organisation’s energy performance each year through effective through-life management, planning, design, procurement, dual-use research, monitoring and measurement. The course will aim to establish a pool of experts, trained to a common standard. Through attendance of the agreed DEMC II Trainings, the participants will be trained to the required technical standard to deliver practical, cost-effective solutions and, uniquely, will benefit from case-specific mentoring support to their first project delivered within the context of their normal work activities. After the Training, they should have sufficient knowledge to further develop their skills in a continuous cycle of self-improvement through on-going mentoring, with permanent access to its established on-line resources.

title: HUB for EU DEFENCE INNOVATION (HEDI): Technology watch, landscaping, foresight - Military Utility assessment - Market consultation - Defence Innovation management courses (online Information Session 27 May 2025)
description: In the context of the Hub for EU Defence Innovation, EDA intends to launch a tender to procure consultancy services in support of technology scouting, technology watch and landscaping, and military utility assessment, including market consultations, as well as defence innovation education and training. As part of the forthcoming tender, EDA is organising an information session on 27 May 2025. The services are structured in 4 LOTS: LOT 1: Technology Watch and Landscaping: Provision of a regular and structured AI supported assessment of worldwide technological developments across both defence and non-defence sectors, identifying emerging trends, weak signals, and dual-use innovations that could impact EU security and defence; LOT 2: Military Utility Assessment: Focuses on evaluating the potential military applications of emerging technologies, assessing their operational utility, and identifying pathways for adoption into defence capability development; LOT 3: Market Research and Market Consultation: Provision of expert consultancy support for conducting market research and facilitating structured market consultations to bridge gaps between innovation suppliers and defence users; LOT 4: Defence Innovation Training Courses: Development and delivery of a structured, high-quality Defence Innovation Course. The first specific contract will focus on an Intermediate Level while potential follow-up contracts will address Basic and Advanced levels. The course is aimed at fostering a harmonized understanding of defence innovation across EU Member States while equipping participants with practical skills for managing and implementing innovation projects within innovation ecosystems. LOT 1 to 3 are services within the HEDI portfolio, the so-called “Defence Frontier Insights”. The Defence Frontier Insights (DFI) service is a key component of the portfolio of activities in HEDI. By scanning and analysing advancements across both defence and non-defence industries and research organizations, DFI serves as an early identification system for technologies and their potential application which could impact the EU security and defence landscape (from both – defensive and offensive perspectives). This service not only identifies new players and technologies but also tracks weak signals that may indicate longer-term trends in the technological environment. Through DFI, HEDI aims at providing a wide spectrum actionable intelligence that informs various aspects of the innovation process: Research & Technology: By keeping a pulse on the latest research developments (i.e. weak signals analysis, patent landscaping, emerging dual-use areas, industrial and institutional reports), DFI is to provide a systemic EU (and worldwide) outlook that complements and augments efforts at the national level, ensuring that MS remain informed and up to date on potentially disruptive military technologies. Capability driven prioritization: DFI is to outline how technological innovations can potentially be transformed into actionable defence capabilities. By integrating findings from R&T and innovation pipelines, the service is to provide insights on the operational utility of new technologies, contributing through other HEDI/EDA services to a long-term capability development planning. Innovation ecosystem definition: DFI is to map out innovation ecosystems’ maturity and ability to accommodate innovation, identifying key players assessing technological readiness levels, and potential barriers to adoption, including legal consultancy, and to identify the most suitable areas for targeted support by other EDA (and wider – EU) working bodies.

title: Quantum Technologies in Defence (Action Plan and Foundational Research for Quantum Technologies in Defence)
description: In the context of Technology and Innovation, EDA intends to launch a tender to develop an Action Plan and Foundational Research for Quantum Technologies in Defence. There will be 2 LOTS: LOT 1: Development and Implementation of the Action plan on Quantum: This lot aims to manage administrative aspects of the ‘Quantum Action Plan’ to be developed for the RTI (Research Technology & Innovation) directorate, propose and consult experts, organize workshops, assist EDA Project Officers in general management of tasks, propose a structure for the Quantum Action Plan, draft the Action Plan and its annexes including roadmap(s) proposal(s) ; LOT 2: Launching Quantum Defence Projects for Foundational Research and Technology: Under this lot economic operators will provide services to identify, propose, and develop promising technologies to different CapTechs or within cross CapTechs activities. The objective is to support the initiation or continuation of R&T projects, and to act as an incubator for early-stage innovations. This could include supporting the first steps of EDA OB studies, Cat. B projects and/or EDF projects or the transition from EDA OB studies to Cat. B projects and/or EDF projects and propose next steps including roadmaps and demonstrations. As part of the forthcoming tender, EDA is organizing an information session on 07 May 2025.

title: Service Framework Contract for the provision of guarding, surveillance, access control and other related services
description: Framework contract for the provision of guarding, surveillance, access control and other related services at EDA premises in Brussels. The performance of the services includes, inter alia, the following tasks: • Provide appropriate identity and access control for Agency staff, suppliers and visitors, • Provide appropriate identity and access control for vehicles and in-depth vehicle security screening, • Produce, programme, register, distribute and destroy identification badges for staff, suppliers, visitors and others entering EDA premises with the use of EDA equipment and software, • Control, process and screen deliveries, mail and shipments to the Agency, • Conduct baggage searches of Agency staff, suppliers and visitors, to prevent weapons and explosives on EDA premises and to prevent unauthorised removal of classified information, valuable objects or other material, • Escort visitors and suppliers, • Monitor deliveries or on-site works, • Monitor alarms, intrusion detection systems and cameras and take appropriate action, • patrol EDA premises to check for unauthorised persons and to enforce internal security rules, • Guard and protect areas/offices where classified meetings are held, • Prevent unauthorised use of electronic equipment, such as mobile phones, cameras or unauthorised laptops, • Guard and control offices and meeting rooms where classified meeting are held, • Open and lock buildings, • Manage keys and codes, • Manage and operate alarm systems, • Devise actions to be taken in case of specific incidents or alarms, • Carry out first interventions in case of fire and accidents, • Participate in heightening safety and security awareness, • Report incidents to Agency’s competent personnel • Use IT equipment for routine operations on EDA systems. Services concern the staff categories defined in the collective labour agreements relating to Joint Committee 317 for guard services in Belgium.

title: Service Framework Contract for the provision of a Proof of concept on integration of AI in M&S enabled wargaming (24.RTI.OP.202)
description: The domain selected for the 2024 Proof-of-Concept under HEDI is the Digital domain with a specific focus the exploration of the role of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in modelling and simulation (M&S) enabled wargaming (WG). M&S-enabled WG provides significant advantages to military end-users by creating realistic and controlled environments in which to test and refine strategies without the risks and costs associated with live training exercises. Additionally, wargaming facilitates the evaluation of new tactics and technologies, enabling military operators to adapt to evolving warfare landscapes swiftly. The ability to replicate diverse combat situations and iterate through multiple scenarios ensures that personnel are well-versed in handling a wide range of contingencies, ultimately leading to improved mission success rates and reduced casualties. The integration of AI into M&S-enabled WG could bring transformative benefits. AI enhances the realism and complexity of simulated environments by generating dynamic and adaptive threat scenarios that evolve based on the actions of the participants. This capability ensures that military operators face unpredictable and challenging situations, closely mimicking real-world conditions. AI-driven simulations can analyse vast amounts of data in real-time, providing immediate feedback and strategic recommendations, which significantly enhances the learning experience. Furthermore, AI facilitates advanced data analytics, offering deeper insights into performance metrics and enabling more precise assessments of tactics and strategies. By incorporating AI, wargaming not only becomes more efficient and effective but also fosters innovation and continuous improvement in military training and operations, ensuring that forces are better prepared for the complexities of modern warfare.

title: “Study on Artificial Intelligence for Missiles & Munitions (AIM&M)” - 24.RTI.OP.212
description: The objective of the Framework Contract is to support EDA and Member States in elaborating the implementation of the CapTech Missiles & Munitions (CapTech M&M) Strategic Research Agenda (SRA) regarding the technological development in AI technologies and how to integrate such into the development of M&M systems. The framework contract shall provide an overview of which areas within the defined areas of interest of the CapTech are interesting to review deeper and are interesting for AI and ML. Areas to be examined if suitable are the Technical Building Blocks (TBB’s) from the CapTech SRA: • Munition Life Management • Insensitive Munitions • Fuzing & Ignition Systems • Precision Guided Munition & Missiles • High Performance Gun Launch • Improved Tools and Methods for Qualification & Safety • ED Detection and Defeat Technologies • High Performance Energetic Materials • Improved Warhead and Penetrator Design • Technologies for Decoying and Obscuring • New Production Technologies for Munition Components • Education & Training • High performance missile propulsion The list of TBB’s is a starting point but not an absolute list that must be strictly followed. Its purpose is to create a link to the CapTech SRA, obtain engagement from the Cap Tech M&M community and be a support for the Workshop (hybrid or on-line), which shall be held (see Task 1.5 below). The result from the framework contract shall support the Member States in planning future usage of AI in M&M including relevant applications for research and development. Also to: • Identify collaborative opportunities addressing M&M. • Support implementation of the relevant Capability Development Priorities by validating technical options for enhanced autonomy and increased performance that could be considered within the relevant Priority Implementation Roadmaps

Description: The objective of the Framework Contract is to support EDA and Member States in elaborating the implementation of the CapTech Missiles & Munitions (CapTech M&M) Strategic Research Agenda (SRA) regarding the technological development in AI technologies and how to integrate such into the development of M&M systems. The framework contract shall provide an overview of which areas within the defined areas of interest of the CapTech are interesting to review deeper and are interesting for AI and ML. Areas to be examined if suitable are the Technical Building Blocks (TBB’s) from the CapTech SRA: • Munition Life Management • Insensitive Munitions • Fuzing & Ignition Systems • Precision Guided Munition & Missiles • High Performance Gun Launch • Improved Tools and Methods for Qualification & Safety • ED Detection and Defeat Technologies • High Performance Energetic Materials • Improved Warhead and Penetrator Design • Technologies for Decoying and Obscuring • New Production Technologies for Munition Components • Education & Training • High performance missile propulsion The list of TBB’s is a starting point but not an absolute list that must be strictly followed. Its purpose is to create a link to the CapTech SRA, obtain engagement from the Cap Tech M&M community and be a support for the Workshop (hybrid or on-line), which shall be held (see Task 1.5 below). The result from the framework contract shall support the Member States in planning future usage of AI in M&M including relevant applications for research and development. Also to: • Identify collaborative opportunities addressing M&M. • Support implementation of the relevant Capability Development Priorities by validating technical options for enhanced autonomy and increased performance that could be considered within the relevant Priority Implementation Roadmaps

title: Framework Contract for the Provision of Services “Ensuring accessibility and availability of Civilian Transport Infrastructure for Military Platforms”_24.CAP.OP.160
description: The overarching objective of the Framework Contract (FWC) is to support EU Member States in ensuring accessibility and availability of civilian transport infrastructure for military platforms. To this end, the FWC should identify gaps and deficits in logistical capacity related to military transport needs, as well as procedural aspects related to military transport in various dimensions, mapping the current situation and providing EU Member States with information that would serve to improve their Military Mobility capabilities. Moreover, this knowledge will ultimately enable the Agency to propose relevant and concrete actions which will enhance Military Mobility related capability development activities. The overarching objective of the FWC will be achieved through specific contracts (SCs) in the various distinct areas related to logistic capacity, including but not limited to: • Landscaping of capability gaps in logistic capacity for the different forms of transportation (land, air, sea, inland water ways); • Landscaping the legislative framework applicable to movement of military assets; • Assessing the potential for improving the above mentioned capacity; • Providing recommendations for future activities on improved accessibility of civilian transport infrastructure for military purposes.

title: OSRA Cluster_24.RTI.OP.185
description: Research & Technology (R&T) provides a critical contribution to the preparation of future capabilities. Together with innovative solutions developed by different defence actors, it brings real and tangible operational benefits to MS’ armed forces. Europe’s defence systems have been developed thanks to major R&T investments that, given the length of development cycles, were made decades ago. To accomplish its mission as defined in Council Decision (CFSP) 2015/1835, EDA promotes, facilitates and manages R&T activities within 15 technology domains (Capability Technology groups – CapTechs ) in order to develop knowledge and technologies needed for future defence capabilities. A CapTech is a working group dedicated to a particular technology area (Area of Responsibility – AoR) linked to the EDA R&T taxonomy. The core task of a CapTech is to gather inputs from the MS experts in order to identify technology gaps and common areas of interest for cooperation. Non-governmental experts (e.g. industries, universities, small and medium enterprises – SMEs, research centres) also contribute to the discussions with ideas for innovation and the most up-to-date technology trends. The purpose of a CapTech is to propose R&T activities in response to agreed defence capability needs and to generate collaborative R&T projects accordingly within a specific technological scope. The CapTechs also contribute to the preparation of projects and programmes not carried out within the CapTech framework, as e.g. in the frame of the European Defence Fund (EDF), with their expertise whenever required. Up to six (6) different types of contracts, with a combined maximum envelope of EUR 2,5 Mill are envisaged under the “OSRA” Cluster: LOT I: CapTech Air Strategic Research Agenda (ref. 24.RTI.OP.186), LOT II: CapTech Maritime Strategic Research Agenda Agenda (ref. 24.RTI.OP.190) & LOT III: CapTech CBRN Strategic Research (ref. 24.RTI.OP.191) The scope of these Direct Contracts is the provision of the “Update or development of the CapTechs’ Strategic Research Agendas”. The SRAs update will comprehensively cover the following aspects across all domains: - Implement the new template for SRA resulting from the OSRA v3 framework. - Document information. - Update the existing sections and contents (e.g., Executive Summary to reflect the current state of the art – technology landscaping, gap analysis, TBBs, conclusions) ensuring their accuracy and alignment with the OSRA v3 guidelines. - TBB roadmaps. - CapTech mission and objectives. Update the CapTech mission, objectives, and AoR based on the EDA Defence Technology Taxonomy v2. - State of the art and gap analysis. - Identify cross-CapTech activities. - Identify the innovation needs, approach and expected activities in line with the “Hub for EU Defence Innovation” (HEDI) services. LOT IV: FWC CapTech Foresight Workshops (ref. 24.RTI.OP.192 & 24.RTI.SC.193) The primary objective of this FWC study is to support the definition and the implementation of the OSRA via a rigorous Technology Foresight activity, adding further to the RTI long-term vision of advanced technologies exploitation in EU defence. This will be accomplished through a series of foresight exercises and related thematic workshops, each concentrating on selected emerging technologies and their impact on future defence capabilities. LOT V: FWC in support of the Action Plan on Autonomous Systems (ref. 24.RTI.OP.194 & 24.RTI.SC.195) The general objective of this FWC is the provision of support to the continued and ongoing implementation of the APAS, through specific activities. Description: Research & Technology (R&T) provides a critical contribution to the preparation of future capabilities. Together with innovative solutions developed by different defence actors, it brings real and tangible operational benefits to MS’ armed forces. Europe’s defence systems have been developed thanks to major R&T investments that, given the length of development cycles, were made decades ago. To accomplish its mission as defined in Council Decision (CFSP) 2015/1835, EDA promotes, facilitates and manages R&T activities within 15 technology domains (Capability Technology groups – CapTechs ) in order to develop knowledge and technologies needed for future defence capabilities. A CapTech is a working group dedicated to a particular technology area (Area of Responsibility – AoR) linked to the EDA R&T taxonomy. The core task of a CapTech is to gather inputs from the MS experts in order to identify technology gaps and common areas of interest for cooperation. Non-governmental experts (e.g. industries, universities, small and medium enterprises – SMEs, research centres) also contribute to the discussions with ideas for innovation and the most up-to-date technology trends. The purpose of a CapTech is to propose R&T activities in response to agreed defence capability needs and to generate collaborative R&T projects accordingly within a specific technological scope. The CapTechs also contribute to the preparation of projects and programmes not carried out within the CapTech framework, as e.g. in the frame of the European Defence Fund (EDF), with their expertise whenever required. Up to six (6) different types of contracts, with a combined maximum envelope of EUR 2,5 Mill are envisaged under the “OSRA” Cluster: LOT I: CapTech Air Strategic Research Agenda (ref. 24.RTI.OP.186), LOT II: CapTech Maritime Strategic Research Agenda Agenda (ref. 24.RTI.OP.190) & LOT III: CapTech CBRN Strategic Research (ref. 24.RTI.OP.191) The scope of these Direct Contracts is the provision of the “Update or development of the CapTechs’ Strategic Research Agendas”. The SRAs update will comprehensively cover the following aspects across all domains: - Implement the new template for SRA resulting from the OSRA v3 framework. - Document information. - Update the existing sections and contents (e.g., Executive Summary to reflect the current state of the art – technology landscaping, gap analysis, TBBs, conclusions) ensuring their accuracy and alignment with the OSRA v3 guidelines. - TBB roadmaps. - CapTech mission and objectives. Update the CapTech mission, objectives, and AoR based on the EDA Defence Technology Taxonomy v2. - State of the art and gap analysis. - Identify cross-CapTech activities. - Identify the innovation needs, approach and expected activities in line with the “Hub for EU Defence Innovation” (HEDI) services. LOT IV: FWC CapTech Foresight Workshops (ref. 24.RTI.OP.192 & 24.RTI.SC.193) The primary objective of this FWC study is to support the definition and the implementation of the OSRA via a rigorous Technology Foresight activity, adding further to the RTI long-term vision of advanced technologies exploitation in EU defence. This will be accomplished through a series of foresight exercises and related thematic workshops, each concentrating on selected emerging technologies and their impact on future defence capabilities. LOT V: FWC in support of the Action Plan on Autonomous Systems (ref. 24.RTI.OP.194 & 24.RTI.SC.195) The general objective of this FWC is the provision of support to the continued and ongoing implementation of the APAS, through specific activities. LOT VI: FWC in support of the AI Action Plan (ref. 24.RTI.OP.267 & 24.RTI.SC.328) The general objective of this FWC is the provision of support to the continued and ongoing implementation of the AI Action Plan, through specific activities.

description: This FWC, and the related specific contracts, will provide support to activities approved through the 3YPF – as it stands now and will develop in the future, within the boundaries of the budget authorized thereby. It addresses a cluster of capability development activities by aggregating different lines of development in the area of Cyber ETE. title: Procurement Cluster: Enablers for Safe Integration of Military Air Capabilities in the European Sky
description: Military operations rely heavily on secure and unhindered access to airspace. This access is crucial for all aircraft types, from traditional manned aircraft to the newest unmanned aircraft systems (UAS). However, the growing complexity of airspace usage, with the introduction of novel technologies and evolving military tactics, presents a significant challenge. Recognizing this complexity, the European Defence Agency (EDA) has taken a leading role in promoting safe airspace integration. The "ENABLERS FOR SAFE AIRSPACE INTEGRATION OF MILITARY AIR CAPABILITIES IN THE EUROPEAN SKY " represents a significant initiative aimed at equipping European militaries for efficient and secure airspace access. This cluster initiative encompasses four distinct projects, each tackling specific aspects of safe airspace integration: • Technology Development (Lot 1) : This project focuses on developing and testing new technologies that facilitate seamless and safe integration of UAS into shared airspace. • UAS Risk Assessment (Lot 2): This project tackles the crucial task of assessing the risks posed by, and to, unmanned aerial systems operating within shared airspace. • High-Altitude Operations (Lot 3): This project addresses security and defence challenges and opportunities associated with operations conducted at high altitudes. • Need-assessment and Market research (Lot 4): this project aims at collecting the requirements of UAS end-users, conducting state of the art review and conduction a market research to propose future projects scopes on UAS airspace integration.

Description: Military operations rely heavily on secure and unhindered access to airspace. This access is crucial for all aircraft types, from traditional manned aircraft to the newest unmanned aircraft systems (UAS). However, the growing complexity of airspace usage, with the introduction of novel technologies and evolving military tactics, presents a significant challenge. Recognizing this complexity, the European Defence Agency (EDA) has taken a leading role in promoting safe airspace integration. The "ENABLERS FOR SAFE AIRSPACE INTEGRATION OF MILITARY AIR CAPABILITIES IN THE EUROPEAN SKY " represents a significant initiative aimed at equipping European militaries for efficient and secure airspace access. This cluster initiative encompasses four distinct projects, each tackling specific aspects of safe airspace integration: • Technology Development (Lot 1) : This project focuses on developing and testing new technologies that facilitate seamless and safe integration of UAS into shared airspace. • UAS Risk Assessment (Lot 2): This project tackles the crucial task of assessing the risks posed by, and to, unmanned aerial systems operating within shared airspace. • High-Altitude Operations (Lot 3): This project addresses security and defence challenges and opportunities associated with operations conducted at high altitudes. • Need-assessment and Market research (Lot 4): this project aims at collecting the requirements of UAS end-users, conducting state of the art review and conduction a market research to propose future projects scopes on UAS airspace integration.

title: Procurement Cluster: Enablers for Safe Integration of Military Air Capabilities in the European Sky - Information Session 4 July 2024 (online)
description: In the context of the cluster of Unmanned Aircraft Systems (UAS) related projects that aim at providing the sought “UAS Enablers for Safe Airspace Integration in European Skyes”, the European Defence Agency (EDA) intends to launch a tender with four lots to support the progress of safe airspace integration of UAS, from low level to high altitude operations (HAO). -------- As part of the forthcoming tender, EDA is organising an information session 04 July 2024, to be held virtually, via WebEx (see below additional information). -------- Lot 1: UAS Single European Sky Experimental Integration: In a drive to elevate the capabilities of European-made low-cost tactical UAS for precision navigation, the new project focuses on two key objectives. Firstly, it seeks to enhance their operational resilience in challenging environments for safe airspace integration – specifically those with limited or denied GNSS access and potential electronic jamming threats. Secondly, the project will leverage recent breakthroughs in EU space-based services alongside onboard sensor fusion powered by artificial intelligence. This integration aims to achieve unwavering navigation accuracy regardless of spectrum availability, demonstrably validating its effectiveness through real-world proof-of-concept and demonstration phases. The successful development of these advanced navigation capabilities for UAS aims to ensure their safe integration into the airspace. --------Lot 2: Risk Assessment for UAS operations: The objective of this lot is to expand the current online tool supporting the MIL-UAS-SPECIFIC methodology (see EDA webpage https://eda.europa.eu/mil-uas-specific-study) to automatize most of the risk assessment process by leveraging the – regularly updated - MIL-UAS-SPECIFIC methodology or any other harmonised Risk assessment methodology accepted by the military (e.g., SORA). The current online tool will become a “networking/connecting” online tool, with selectable Risk assessment methodologies running back office, including a selectable accepted risk level for the UAS operations to cover operations in peace, crisis and war times. -------- Lot 3: Higher Airspace Operations (HAO) study: HAO have been in the spotlight. The upcoming EASA regulatory work requires that the civil–military aspects are included. The objective is to clarify specific civil–military aspects in the domain of HAO in order to: a) analyse the security risks; b) Address potential challenges in order to avoid any adverse impact on national security and defence capabilities with an EU approach; c) Ensure military access to higher airspace. Take advantage of all opportunities, particularly those offered by the civil-military collaboration make the most of the identified synergies. -------- Lot 4: Consultancy services for needs assessment, market research and consultation, analysis of the state-of-the-art: The surge in small and mid-sized UAS operating under the “specific” category of operations, is prompting collaboration between authorities, regulators, and UAS operators to ensure safe integration into existing airspace. This project aims to bridge the gap by assessing the specific needs of military UAS users and leverage the dual-use technology towards the safe integration into European airspace. This project has two key objectives: a) to understand end-user needs for safe airspace integration. b) to evaluate technologies for enhanced UAS integration, including the analysis of state-of-the-art of current conspicuity, ATM and positioning technologies within the EU market, that can enable safe UAS integration. c) the organisation of market consultation sessions with stakeholders

title: Service Framework Contract for the Provision of ‘Data Centric Security and Zero Trust Architecture Technologies (DARC)’
description: DARC pursues the general objective of EDA pMS in identifying the technology challenges but also non-technology ones but with an impact on technology, towards the implementation of DCS and ZTA, especially in hybrid environments of both locally hosted and cloud-based infrastructure. The focus of this general objective must be the application of DCS and ZTA in military environments and the provision of relevant use cases. The analysis, findings and results shall provide tangible solutions and actionable recommendations for near-term adoption when possible and propose specific roadmap for mid-term adoption in cases that near-term is not feasible. Especially in the Defence and under the context of multi-domain operations (MDO) and associated command and control (C2) systems, sharing of data through various means between the involved armed forces in a secure and controlled way for the appropriate required period, is crucial for mission success.

title: Service Framework Contract for the Provision of Hybrid Multifunctional Metamaterials for Defence Applications (HiMMODA)
description: Hybrid multifunctional metamaterials — once available — will have superior functionality as compared to ‘single-function’ metamaterials, combining several functions (e.g. in Optronics and Radio Frequency domains) in one module, which could lead to benefits in terms of size, weight and power — and cost (SWAP-C).The main objective of this project is to study and analyse the application of hybrid multifunctional metamaterials in defence areas identified. The goal is the development of a unique proof of concept, that is responsive, via the utilisation of suitable metamaterials, to challenging multifunctionality requirements. The proof of concept shall be modular, in order to be adapted to various requirement configurations.

title: Study on the Impact of (other than REACH/CLP) European Chemical/Waste Regulations on the Defence Sector
description: The study shall provide detailed information on the impact on defence of the 5 EU Chemical Regulations, as well as their interactions/consistency with REACH and CLP and between them, towards a more consistent approach in overall EU legislation for chemicals, for defence stakeholders, aiming among others:— to address defence specificities (exemptions/exclusions/, etc.) as foreseen in the legal texts of the regulations,— to assess the impact of the regulations on defence and to develop recommendations for related mitigation actions,— to support avoiding in the future undesired regulatory outcomes impacting defence in multi-regulation situations (e.g. regrettable substitution of chemical substance).
